_about: Drafted by Claude on 2026-11-24 (E3, prompt 74); approved by Nav on 2026-11-24 (prompt 75). Ceres's 30 fun facts for the Destination file card and /destinations/ceres, one a day, in the same format as mars.json. Every fact was checked on 2026-11-24 against the NASA page in 'source'; 'quote' is the supporting text from that page (' … ' joins two parts of the same page). None repeats a milestone fact (content/milestones/ceres.json).

facts.fact: Ceres is the largest object in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter.
facts.quote: Dwarf planet Ceres is the largest object in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter.

facts.fact: Ceres is the only dwarf planet in the inner Solar System.
facts.quote: Ceres is the only dwarf planet in the inner solar system.

facts.fact: Giuseppe Piazzi spotted Ceres in 1801. It was the first member of the asteroid belt ever found.
facts.quote: Ceres was the first member of the asteroid belt to be discovered when Giuseppe Piazzi spotted it in 1801.

facts.fact: Piazzi was searching for a star when he found Ceres, and he called it a planet.
facts.quote: Giuseppe Piazzi discovers Ceres while searching for a star and calls it a planet.

facts.fact: Ceres was first called a planet, then an asteroid. In 2006 it became a dwarf planet, along with Pluto and Eris.
facts.quote: Ceres was initially classified as a planet and later classified as an asteroid … Ceres was designated a dwarf planet in 2006 along with Pluto and Eris.

facts.fact: Ceres is named after the Roman goddess of corn and harvests.
facts.quote: Ceres is named for the Roman goddess of corn and harvests.

facts.fact: The word "cereal" comes from the same name as Ceres.
facts.quote: The word cereal comes from the same name.

facts.fact: Ceres is about 940 km across.
facts.quote: Ceres is approximately 585 miles (940 kilometers) across.

facts.fact: If Earth were the size of a US nickel coin, Ceres would be about as big as a poppy seed.
facts.quote: If Earth were the size of a nickel, Ceres would be about as big as a poppy seed.

facts.fact: A day on Ceres lasts about 9 hours, one of the shortest days in the Solar System.
facts.quote: it completes one rotation every 9 hours, making its day length one of the shortest in the solar system.

facts.fact: Ceres's axis is tilted just 4 degrees, so it doesn't have seasons like more tilted planets do.
facts.quote: Ceres' axis of rotation is tilted just 4 degrees with respect to the plane of its orbit around the Sun. … doesn't experience seasons like other more tilted planets do.

facts.fact: Ceres has no moons.
facts.quote: Ceres does not have any moons.

facts.fact: Ceres has no rings.
facts.quote: Ceres does not have any rings.

facts.fact: Ceres could be as much as a quarter water. If so, it holds more water than Earth does.
facts.quote: Ceres could be composed of as much as 25 percent water. … If that is correct, Ceres has more water than Earth does.

facts.fact: Ceres probably has a solid core and a mantle made of water ice.
facts.quote: Ceres probably has a solid core and a mantle made of water ice.

facts.fact: Ceres has a very thin atmosphere, and there is evidence that it contains water vapour.
facts.quote: Ceres has a very thin atmosphere, and there is evidence it contains water vapor.

facts.fact: The water vapour may come from ice volcanoes, or from ice near the surface turning straight into gas.
facts.quote: The vapor may be produced by ice volcanoes or by ice near the surface sublimating

facts.fact: The salts on Ceres aren't table salt. They are other minerals, such as magnesium sulfate.
facts.quote: The salts on Ceres aren’t like table salt (sodium chloride) … are made of different minerals like magnesium sulfate.

facts.fact: Occator Crater is home to the brightest area on Ceres.
facts.quote: Occator Crater, home to the brightest area on Ceres

facts.fact: Ceres is covered in countless small, young craters, and none of them is more than 280 km across.
facts.quote: Ceres is covered in countless small, young craters … none are larger than 175 miles (280 kilometers) in diameter

facts.fact: Shaded spots inside some of Ceres's craters could hold water ice for long periods of time.
facts.quote: could have water ice in them for long periods of time

facts.fact: NASA's Dawn found signs of recent, and maybe still ongoing, activity in several places on Ceres.
facts.quote: Dawn also returned evidence for recent and potentially ongoing activity in several places on Ceres.

facts.fact: Ceres is one of the few places in the Solar System where scientists would like to search for signs of life.
facts.quote: Ceres is one of the few places in our solar system where scientists would like to search for possible signs of life.

facts.fact: Scientists call Ceres an "embryonic planet": Jupiter's strong gravity stopped it becoming a fully formed planet.
facts.quote: Scientists describe Ceres as an "embryonic planet," … Nearby Jupiter's strong gravity prevented it from becoming a fully formed planet.

facts.fact: Ceres formed along with the rest of the Solar System, about 4.5 billion years ago.
facts.quote: Ceres formed along with the rest of the solar system about 4.5 billion years ago

facts.fact: Ammonia found on Ceres hints that its materials, or even Ceres itself, came from the outer Solar System.
facts.quote: the discovery of ammonia on Ceres suggests its materials, or even Ceres itself, came from the outer solar system

facts.fact: Before Dawn arrived, models said Ceres's water was an icy layer wrapped round a rocky mantle, and Hubble backed that up.
facts.quote: Pre-Dawn models suggested Ceres' water would be in the form of an icy layer wrapped around a rocky mantle. … Observations by NASA's Hubble Space Telescope confirmed that model.

facts.fact: Dawn went into orbit around Ceres on 6 March 2015, about four months before New Horizons flew past Pluto.
facts.quote: NASA's Dawn mission went into orbit around Ceres on March 6, 2015, … about four months before New Horizons flew past Pluto on July 14, 2015.

facts.fact: Ceres was the first dwarf planet ever to be orbited by a spacecraft.
facts.quote: Ceres was the first dwarf planet to be orbited by a spacecraft.

facts.fact: In the TV series The Expanse, people live on Ceres.
facts.quote: In the TV series "The Expanse," Ceres is inhabited by humans
